summary: The main article describes a photoactive EDA complex-mediated chromium-catalyzed alkyl addition to aldehydes using alkyl thianthrenium salts. It includes 1 optimization table, 1 preparation scheme, 2 substrate scope figures, and 3 figures detailing mechanistic studies and further applications.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Some selected approved alkyl deuterated drugs.
items.description: Displays chemical structures of FDA-approved deuterated drugs like Deutetrabenazine and Donafenib.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Chromium-catalyzed NHK reactions. a) Development of NHK reactions. b) Desulfurative functionalizations of alkyl thianthrenium salts. c) This work about EDA-induced NHK reaction.
items.description: Compares traditional NHK reactions and previous thianthrenium functionalizations with the current EDA-induced chromium-catalyzed approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Reaction investigation.
items.description: Optimization table screening catalysts, reductants, solvents, and light sources for the alkyl addition reaction.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.caption: Preparation of deuterated alkyl thianthrenium salt.
items.description: Shows the synthesis of deuterated alkyl thianthrenium salts from alcohols using D2O and thianthrene.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.caption: Substrate scope with respect to aldehydes.
items.description: Illustrates the variety of aldehydes (alkyl, aryl, heteroaromatic) compatible with the deuterated alkyl addition.

items.heading: Figure 5
items.caption: Substrate scope with respect to deuterated alkyl thianthrenium salts.
items.description: Shows the scope of different alkyl thianthrenium salts used to produce various beta-deuterated secondary alcohols.

items.heading: Figure 6
items.caption: Mechanism exploration. a) Radical trapping experiment. b) Reaction investigation utilizing stoichiometric amount of chromium catalyst. c) Stern-Volmer uorescene quenching. d) UV-Vis absorption. e) BenesiHildebrand plot. f) Job's plot.
items.description: Presents experimental data supporting the formation of an EDA complex and a radical-mediated mechanism.

items.heading: Figure 7
items.caption: Plausible mechanism.
items.description: Diagrams the proposed catalytic cycle involving EDA complex activation, radical capture by Cr(II), and regeneration of the catalyst by Hantzsch ester.

items.heading: Figure 8
items.caption: Further application: Photoactive chromium-catalyzed three-component reactions.
items.description: Demonstrates a three-component coupling of aryl thianthrenium salts, 1,3-butadiene, and aldehydes to form homoallylic alcohols.
